guideTitle: The Best DisplayLink Docking Stations for Extra Monitors
metaTitle: Best DisplayLink Docking Stations for Triple Monitors (2026)
metaDescription: We compared DisplayLink docks for adding monitors beyond a laptop's native limit, plus native Thunderbolt alternatives, on display output, charging, driver needs and price.
introParagraphs: DisplayLink docks drive extra monitors through a software driver rather than the laptop's own display outputs. That is how a base Apple Silicon MacBook, which natively supports limited external displays, can run three monitors, and how many business laptops add screens beyond their built-in limit.

The trade-offs are a driver to install and keep updated, some processor load, and output that is less suited to color-critical work or protected video. Four DisplayLink docks are compared here, alongside three native alternatives (two Thunderbolt 4 docks and a USB hub) for anyone whose laptop can drive the monitors directly.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $117 to $228 at the time of writing.

wavlink-12-in-1-displaylink-3-monitor.summary: A 12-in-1 DisplayLink dock for three 4K 60Hz monitors with 100W charging.
wavlink-12-in-1-displaylink-3-monitor.description:
The WAVLINK 12-in-1 is the value pick: DisplayLink output for three monitors at up to 4K 60Hz each, with 100W charging, HDMI and DisplayPort outputs, gigabit Ethernet and 5Gbps USB, listed for Dell, HP, Lenovo and MacBook laptops.

It costs about $117 at the time of writing, the least here. A DisplayLink driver is required on first setup.
wavlink-12-in-1-displaylink-3-monitor.bestFor: Adding three monitors on a budget.
wavlink-12-in-1-displaylink-3-monitor.skipIf: You need color-critical output; a native Thunderbolt dock suits that.

anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.summary: A 14-port Anker Prime DisplayLink dock with triple 4K, 140W and a cooling fan.
anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.description:
The Anker Prime DL7400 is the premium DisplayLink option: triple 4K 60Hz output, up to 140W output, 14 ports and a built-in cooling fan for sustained use.

Anker lists it for Windows laptops and requires the latest DisplayLink driver. It is the most expensive dock here at about $228 at the time of writing.
anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.bestFor: Windows desks running three monitors all day.
anker-prime-dl7400-14-port-triple-displa.skipIf: You use a Mac; the Plugable UD-ULTCDL lists macOS support.

plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-mac-displayli.summary: A 13-in-1 Plugable dock with three HDMI outputs via DisplayLink on Mac and 100W charging.
plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-mac-displayli.description:
The Plugable UD-ULTCDL is the pick for a MacBook that needs three monitors: triple HDMI output using the DisplayLink driver on macOS, 100W charging, a 20W secondary USB-C port, gigabit Ethernet, an SD reader and four more USB ports.

It costs about $195 at the time of writing. The macOS DisplayLink app must be installed and allowed screen-recording permission, per DisplayLink's setup process.
pros: Three monitors on a base MacBook
plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-mac-displayli.bestFor: MacBook users who need three monitors.
plugable-ud-ultcdl-13-in-1-mac-displayli.skipIf: Your Mac drives enough displays natively; a Thunderbolt dock avoids DisplayLink.

plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.summary: A triple-display USB dock: one 4K 30Hz and two 1080p 60Hz, for Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.description:
This Plugable dock drives three displays through USB-based video: one 4K at 30Hz and two at 1080p 60Hz, with 100W charging and six 5Gbps USB ports, listed for Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.

The 4K output runs at 30Hz, which feels less smooth for scrolling, and it costs about $160 at the time of writing.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.bestFor: Mixed-OS households or ChromeOS users adding monitors.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-100w.skipIf: You want three 4K 60Hz screens; the WAVLINK lists that for less.

plugable-tbt-udm-native-tb4-alternative.summary: A certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with native dual 4K or single 6K output, not DisplayLink.
plugable-tbt-udm-native-tb4-alternative.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is not a DisplayLink dock: it is a certified Thunderbolt 4 dock that uses the laptop's own graphics, so there is no driver and no DisplayLink compression. It supports dual 4K HDMI or a single 6K display, 100W charging, six USB ports, SD and Ethernet.

It can only drive as many displays as your laptop supports natively.
cons: Limited by laptop's native display count
plugable-tbt-udm-native-tb4-alternative.bestFor: Laptops that natively support the monitors you need.
plugable-tbt-udm-native-tb4-alternative.skipIf: Your laptop supports only one external display and you need more.

dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-native-alternati.summary: Dell's SD25TB4 Thunderbolt 4 smart dock for up to four displays, 130W and 2.5GbE.
dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-native-alternati.description:
The Dell Pro Thunderbolt 4 Smart Dock (SD25TB4) is Dell's native alternative: certified Thunderbolt 4, up to four displays via two DisplayPort 1.4 and HDMI 2.1, 130W charging, 2.5GbE Ethernet and built-in Wi-Fi, validated for Dell Pro laptops.

It costs about $225 at the time of writing. Display count depends on the laptop.
specs: Up to 4 displays (2 x DP 1.4, HDMI 2.1)
dell-pro-tb4-smart-dock-native-alternati.skipIf: You use a non-Dell laptop; the Plugable TBT-UDM is more general.

anker-prime-160w-14-port-usb-alternative.summary: Anker's 14-port Prime with 160W output and native dual 4K, no DisplayLink driver.
anker-prime-160w-14-port-usb-alternative.description:
The Anker Prime 14-port is a middle ground: native dual 4K output without a DisplayLink driver, up to 160W total output, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio, for about $170 at the time of writing.

Like any native dock, it relies on your laptop's display support.
anker-prime-160w-14-port-usb-alternative.bestFor: Two-monitor desks that want to avoid DisplayLink.
anker-prime-160w-14-port-usb-alternative.skipIf: You need three monitors on a base laptop; choose a DisplayLink dock.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Only if your laptop cannot natively drive the number of monitors you want. Otherwise a native dock avoids the driver and trade-offs.
The WAVLINK and Anker DL7400 list three 4K 60Hz; the Plugable multi-OS dock one 4K at 30Hz and two 1080p.
Check driver support: the Anker DL7400 lists Windows; the Plugable UD-ULTCDL lists macOS; the multi-OS Plugable adds ChromeOS.
100W to 160W here; match your laptop's charger.

faq.a: A technology that sends video over USB using a software driver, letting a laptop run more monitors than its native outputs support.
A driver to install and update, some processor load, and limitations with color-critical work and some protected video.

faq.q: Do I need DisplayLink on a Mac?
faq.a: On base Apple Silicon MacBooks with limited native display support, it is the usual way to add several monitors. On Macs that support enough displays natively, a Thunderbolt dock is simpler.

bottomLine: For three monitors on a budget, the WAVLINK is the value DisplayLink dock; the Anker DL7400 adds cooling for all-day Windows use, and the Plugable UD-ULTCDL is the Mac-focused choice.
If your laptop can drive your monitors natively, skip DisplayLink: the Plugable TBT-UDM and Dell SD25TB4 are native Thunderbolt docks, and the Anker Prime 14-port is the no-driver USB option.
